3.3 Future-Guided Evaluation & Refinement
[id=S3.SS3.p1.1] This stage aims to establish a closed-loop interaction between action prediction and future imagination based on the highly shared representation ℋt\mathcal{H}_{t} between the VLA and the world model. DriveWorld-VLA is required not only to predict actions but also to effectively imagine the corresponding future outcomes induced by those actions, and to evaluate and refine actions according to the imagined future states. Given the ℬt\mathcal{B}_{t}, ℋt\mathcal{H}_{t} and 𝒜t−1\mathcal{A}_{t-1}, DriveWorld-VLA first predicts future actions 𝒜t+Δ​t′\mathcal{A}_{t+\Delta t}^{\prime} and generates future imagination ℬt+Δ​t\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t} via the first denoising branch. The predicted actions are subsequently used to condition the second denoising branch, where Euler-based sampling is performed to produce action-conditioned future imagination ℬt+Δ​t′\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{\prime}:
[id=S3.E9]
[id=S3.E9X]
ℬt+Δ​tk+1=ℬt+Δ​tk+1N​(DiTθ​(ℬt′,𝒜t+Δ​t,xk,kN)),\displaystyle\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{k+1}=\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{k}+\frac{1}{N}(\textsc{DiT}_{\theta}(\mathcal{B}_{t}^{\prime},\mathcal{A}_{t+\Delta t},x_{k},\frac{k}{N})),
(9)
[id=S3.SS3.p1.2] where ℬt+Δ​t′=ℬt+Δ​tk+1\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{\prime}=\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{k+1}, and NN denotes the sampling steps and is set to 2525.
[id=S3.SS3.p2.1] To evaluate the quality of predicted actions, we jointly consider the consistency between the action-conditioned imagination ℬt+Δ​t′\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{\prime} and the corresponding future BEV representation ℬt+Δ​t\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}. A learned reward function ℛ\mathcal{R} assigns a scalar score r^t+Δ​t\hat{r}_{t+\Delta t} to each predicted trajectory, with ground-truth rewards obtained by executing the predicted trajectories in a simulator and performing online evaluation. This process can be formulated as,
[id=S3.E10]
[id=S3.E10X]
r^t+Δ​t=ℛ⁡(ℬt+Δ​t′,ℬt+Δ​t,𝒜t+Δ​t′).\displaystyle\hat{r}_{t+\Delta t}=\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t}^{\prime},\mathcal{B}_{t+\Delta t},\mathcal{A}_{t+\Delta t}^{\prime}).
(10)
[id=S3.SS3.p2.2] Beyond trajectory quality assessment, this reward-driven design promotes close-loop between future imagination and action generation. Rather than uniformly supervising all multi-modal predictions, training prioritizes trajectories with higher predicted rewards, reinforcing those that lead to more favorable imagined outcomes and enabling consequence-aware action refinement,
[id=S3.E11]
[id=S3.E11X]

(11)
[id=S3.SS3.p3.1] Supervision. During this stage, DeNoIsEr and VlM are frozen. Training focuses on refining the reward function and the action head. The future BEV latents generated by the two denoising branches are fused and fed into the segmentation decoder for supervised BEV decoding, resulting in three complementary supervision signals:
[id=S3.E12]
[id=S3.E12X]
ℒs3=ℒa​c​t′+ℒs​e​g+ℒr​e​w,\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{s_{3}}=\mathcal{L}_{act}^{\prime}+\mathcal{L}_{seg}+\mathcal{L}_{rew},
(12)
[id=S3.SS3.p3.2] where ℒs​e​g\mathcal{L}_{seg} also supervises the semantic BEV map decoding, ℒa​c​t′\mathcal{L}_{act}^{\prime} supervises the predicted actions weighted by rewards and ℒr​e​w\mathcal{L}_{rew} supervises the reward function ℛ\mathcal{R}.
